title: Formal Laurent series in one variable
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. A \emph{formal Laurent series} in one variable $x$ over $A$ is a family $(a_i)_{i\in\mathbf Z}$ of elements of $A$ for which there is $n_0\in\mathbf Z$ with $a_i=0$ for all $i<n_0$; it is written $\sum_{i}a_ix^i$. The set $A((x))$ of formal Laurent series is a commutative ring with coefficientwise addition and the product $\bigl(\sum_ia_ix^i\bigr)\bigl(\sum_jb_jx^j\bigr)=\sum_k\bigl(\sum_{i+j=k}a_ib_j\bigr)x^k$ (each inner sum is finite since both families vanish below some index). The ring $A[[x]]$ of formal power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] (the case $n=1$) maps to $A((x))$ by $\sum_{i\ge0}a_ix^i\mapsto\sum_ia_ix^i$ with $a_i=0$ for $i<0$; this is an injective ring homomorphism, by which $A[[x]]$ is regarded as the subring of Laurent series with $a_i=0$ for all $i<0$. A nonzero Laurent series $\sum_ia_ix^i$ has an \emph{order} $n=\min\{i: a_i\neq0\}$ and is written $a_nx^n+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+\cdots$ with $a_n\neq0$.
